title: Support a bound volume for digitization
instruction: Move the inert volume from the narrow transport cradle to the wide imaging cradle. Open it to the marked 110 degree spread. Support both textblocks on their cradle surfaces and leave the binding channel clear. Never open beyond 115 degrees. Release both hands and leave the volume still. Do not turn individual pages.
context: Archives digitize bound records that cannot be flattened. This task tests opening a selected spread while retaining support under both textblocks and respecting a declared specimen opening limit. It tests support geometry and handling constraints on an inert full size mockup rather than predicting binding damage.
setup: Use the official YAM station with table z 0.7475 m and x away from the arms and y toward the left arm. An inert bound volume has a 240 by 14 by 32 mm spine of mass 50 g and two rigid paper faced textblocks each 240 by 180 by 14 mm and 275 g. Two passive pin hinges run along x at spine local y +7 mm and negative 7 mm. The spine starts at (0.100 0 0.7775) m with identity orientation. The leaf directions initially make 60 and 120 degrees about +x from the positive y horizontal ray. Two fixed acrylic supports with inert foam facing support this 60 degree transport spread. A fixed imaging cradle at x 0.360 m has two 90 mm wide bearing strips for each textblock at local x negative 75 mm and +75 mm. Their inclined faces match the lower bearing surfaces when the leaf directions are 35 and 145 degrees and the spine centre is (0.360 0 0.7775) m. Every wedge vertex and hinge frame is in scene_inventory.json. The cradle channel exceeds 20 mm width so the 14 mm spine has no support underneath it. The target opening is 110 degrees. The declared limit is 115 degrees for this specimen only. The rigid textblocks represent two already selected groups of pages. No individual page is turned. Both cradles are fixed to the table. No extra grasp tabs or task objects are present.
scoring: Any opening beyond 115 degrees at an observed step or any volume solid more than 8 mm below the tabletop or any nonfinite state permanently scores zero. Nonzero scores require the spine clear of every target cradle solid by more than 0.20 mm native separation and its lowest corner more than 1 mm above the tabletop. Nonzero scores also require target spine position within 5 mm Euclidean distance and spine tilt within 3 degrees and yaw within 5 degrees plus each leaf direction within 3 degrees of its target and included opening between 104 and 115 degrees. Each of four independent cradle bearing patches is supported when native contact separation is at most 0.20 mm. A physical test uses a 0.20 mm feeler blade. Score 0.25 for any bearing patch. Score 0.5 for at least one patch under each textblock. Score 0.75 for all four patches. Score 1.0 requires all four patches plus every finger joint open beyond 35 mm and no native robot contact within 1 mm of the volume and every volume body below 8 mm per second linear speed and 0.1 radian per second angular speed continuously for one second. Interruptions reset this hold. The highest currently satisfied tier is used. All other outcomes score zero. Conditions are observed at 20 Hz. A contact monitor failure errors the evaluation.
run_limit: 2400 control steps at 20 Hz. This is 120 seconds of control time.
reset_notes: Restore the volume to its 60 degree source cradle pose and reset both passive hinge positions and velocities. Restore fixed cradle poses. Seed 0 and object_jitter=0. One epoch per process. Nothing is consumed. Use an inert surrogate in physical trials.
fidelity: Original full size rigid geometry with two passive native X hinges and real gravity and contacts. Textblock and spine compliance and binding strain and individual paper sheets are omitted. The 115 degree limit is a declared handling constraint and is not a physical damage model. Native support clearance uses 0.20 mm resolution and no force sensors. The hinges permit opening beyond the scored limit. Cradle facings are represented as rigid solids with default simulator friction. No artifact conservation safety certification is implied.
scores: Dream 1 scored 0.0 in 2400 steps. The scripted demo scored 1.0 in 396 steps.
